assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only 86-eighty-six:viktor-idinarohk@original-light-novels#86-vika-character-reference-profile, the canonical CMR-5 Viktor Idinarohk (Vika) character reference profile (version 1.2, release 86-V2-V01-V14-1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the locked original-Japanese light novels V01-V14, in which Vika is materially attested from V05, with Alter.1 as audited supplemental ordinary-life evidence and Alter.2 excluded. The profile states that its cumulative diagnostic index holds 205 rows (VIK-001 to VIK-205) across V05-V09, V11-V14 and Alter.1, that five rows reuse Phase-5 locators and the rest are LOCATOR_GAP rows, and that the index, not the prose, is the retrieval surface for exact Japanese anchors. The profile itself lists 22 diagnostic-control entries, single rows or row ranges naming 35 rows, each routed by volume and XHTML file and none to a paragraph; one carries a Phase-5 locator (VIK-176 to VIK-177, V13-L061), and two are given only as the vicinity of a row (VIK-016, VIK-017). That index is not curated evidence on this subject, and no row, count by volume or anchor is taken from it beyond what the profile prints. The CMR-9 promotion audit and ledger, the profile's validation report, the relationship register matrix (including the V12 Frederica row the profile cites), the crosswalk, other characters' profiles (including that of Lerche), the ledgers L01, L02, L05, L07 and L09, Documents 06-09, 11, 12 and 18, the canonical V06 reading the profile cites, the Phase-5 and Phase-8 artifacts and the Japanese EPUBs are not curated evidence on this subject either, and nothing is borrowed from them. The profile's CMR-9 verdict and its High, Moderate and Open labels are inputs, not conclusions. No anime adaptation, V15+ volume or Alter.2 scene is included, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The profile's developmental states from V05 through the V14 boundary. Childhood loss of his mother (the failed resurrection at five, V05 p-004) and the death of Lercheritt, his hereditary servant and companion (V05 p-007), are memories he holds in every state, not selectable present states. Present states: V05 (p-002 to p-010: family smile, teasing Lerche, monster self-description over her broken body); V06 creator power made partially self-limiting (p-005: no backup and no absolute obedience for Lerche, and the diagnosis of Shin (Shinei Nouzen); p-006: the apology to Yanina, a Sirin; p-009: the family blacklist); V07 inherited status retained as chosen form (p-007, そう在りたい); V09 postwar university possibility (p-004); V12 (p-008, Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort)); V13 chosen political stake with the Eighty-Six (p-005, 俺の意思だ, V13-L061); and V14 forced trauma replay (p-006). V08 has 20 index rows and V11 has 9, but neither has a listed control. Alter.1 rows (part0041 to part0057) are supplements without volume placement. No default state is set, controls reach only a file, and states after V14 are not established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The profile gives a detailed account of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk): mechanism-first, causally hungry cognition with low conventional taboo sensitivity, model-before-sympathize under uncertainty, solvability as an intervention trigger, fast analytic compression, failure handled by revising the model, and moral repair by constraining future power rather than narrating purity. Where attachment or accepted authority is present it discriminates: he commands Lerche but does not override her privacy claim (V06 p-005, VIK-065), treats Sirins as a class with weapon logic plus individuating recognition (V06 p-006, VIK-078), takes a political stake for the Eighty-Six as his own choice (V13 p-005, VIK-176 to VIK-177), and interrogates a prohibition's scope unless he accepts its authority and purpose (V06 p-009, VIK-084). B would overclaim: the profile's governing conclusion locates his defining tension at power versus answer-space, and for the case it calls his largest ethical hazard, a person or artificial subject he can treat as a solvable problem without attachment, it names the deciding question (whether he establishes standing or only feasibility) and offers only a trend, that development makes the question harder to bypass. How far his creator ethics generalize beyond Lerche, and whether he accepts peer constraints in a high-stakes scientific dispute, are MODERATE. That is competing motives left unranked inside the core, not uncertainty about wording or affect. D would understate an explicit decision grammar, located state deltas and relation-specific rules that support narrow conditional prediction.

The profile orders the development of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) with causes: the childhood rule that correct method yields the correct result, broken by the failed resurrection of his mother (V05 p-004); first fear and the plea to Lercheritt not to leave him (V05 p-007, VIK-042 to VIK-044); V05-V06 creator power made partially self-limiting, with no backup and no absolute obedience for Lerche (V06 p-005, VIK-065); V07 inherited royalty retained as chosen form (p-007, VIK-091); V09 a postwar future outside duty becomes imaginable (p-004, VIK-131); V13 solidarity as a chosen stake (p-005, VIK-177); and V14 the correction of 'fearless' by a trauma response he functions through (p-006, VIK-184). It forbids regressions, such as treating death as casually reversible after V05-V06 or claiming he has no fear after V14. C would understate an ordered, causally explained sequence with located turns. A is rejected: V08 and V11 have no listed control, no turn is routed to a paragraph, and nothing after V14 is established.

The profile fixes the frame of the written-Japanese register of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk): stable first person 俺 under an aristocratic and intellectual register; 卿 toward officers and peers in an aristocratic-professional frame, お前 in familiar or command contexts and 貴様 under irritation or battle pressure; technical speech that becomes more exact, not more polite; situational rather than total royal language; insult as familiarity (七歳児 to Lerche, V05 p-005, VIK-024); and the rule that deepest affect simplifies rather than elaborates (あいたかったから, V05 p-004; そう在りたい, V07 p-007; 俺の意思だ, V13 p-005; ご苦労 and すまない, V06 p-006). B would overclaim: the profile gives no sentence-ending, particle or lexicon profile, no exemplar reaches a paragraph, the お飾り to 卿 shift toward Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort) rests on a matrix row outside the set, and the L09 voice ledger and Document 12 that it relies on are outside the set. D would understate a located pronoun and address system with state rules and four located simplification exemplars.

Ordinary conduct of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) is located mainly in Alter.1: chess with Shin (Shinei Nouzen) that he keeps playing after losing his superiority (part0041, VIK-195 to VIK-196), quietly shielding Lena (Vladilena Milizé) from embarrassment (part0044), a luxurious royal room almost empty of possessions (part0046), and declining a politically loaded gift in favor of arranging private time for Lena and Shin (part0057, VIK-203 to VIK-205), with the V09 university possibility (p-004). The drivers are stated: competitive pique, tact enacted by fixing the condition rather than narrating the feeling, and a status that changes what ordinary gestures do. B would overclaim: the mainline ordinary sample is thin, the Alter.1 scenes have no volume placement, and items such as coffee and the V12 caterpillar impulse have no listed control. D would understate stated drivers with located ordinary conduct.

Eleven directed relations of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) are analyzed with distinct rules: Lerche, commanded but not overridden at her privacy boundary, with rough familiarity (V05 p-005; V06 p-005); Lercheritt, the least defended register, inside an acknowledged caste asymmetry (V05 p-007; Alter.1 part0046); Shin (Shinei Nouzen), from anomaly and mirror to peer, met with premise attack and pettiness rather than comfort (V06 p-005; Alter.1 part0041); Lena (Vladilena Milizé), status-aware logistical care (Alter.1 part0044 and part0057); Zafar (Zafar Idinarohk), his older brother, and his father the king, the only recipients of a childlike smile (V05 p-002; V09 p-004) and authorities who contain him (V06 p-009); Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), challenged rather than reassured (V12 p-008); the Eighty-Six, instrumental legibility joined to personal commitment (V13 p-005); and the Sirins as a class, weapon logic with individuating recognition (V06 p-006). C would understate this recipient-specific discrimination. A is rejected: Annette (Annette Penrose), Zelene, a speaking Legion intelligence, and his father as a policy authority have no listed control of their own, reverse directions are not analyzed, and the matrix and L02 are outside the set.

Private states of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) are located across states with causes: the child-simple wish to see his mother and the absence that drove the resurrection attempt (V05 p-004); first fear at being left behind by Lercheritt, recognized by him as selfish, and the plea to stay (V05 p-007); observing that he feels essentially nothing before Lerche's broken body and naming himself a monster (V05 p-010, VIK-051); the V14 trauma replay he bites through and later does not want recalled (p-006, VIK-184); and guilt toward Lercheritt's family (Alter.1 part0046). The profile separates categories where his affect is low from attachment categories where it is not. A would overclaim: V06-V13 interior is read mostly from speech and action, how far he understands the monster self-description as defensive is MODERATE, and no interior passage reaches a paragraph. C would understate located interior states across childhood memory, V05 and V14 that the profile ties to his choices.

The profile states how Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) disagrees by interlocutor: with intellectual peers he attacks the premise rather than the surface claim (the V06 diagnosis of Shin (Shinei Nouzen), p-005, VIK-069); with institutional authority he works inside status while testing its limits, so that his family closes interpretive loopholes in writing (V06 p-009, VIK-084); with subordinates command can be absolute but sometimes deliberately is not (V06 p-005, VIK-065); and with distressed peers diagnosis comes before comfort, which can help or wound. Anger compresses commands and raises rough address. C would understate conditioned response families with located controls. A is rejected: the V06 Shin exchange is the one full interpersonal conflict listed, conflict with a peer authority in a high-stakes scientific dispute is MODERATE, and the anger and battle-register claims have no listed control.

The profile gives Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) located positions: refusal has value when it is not architecturally impossible, so Lerche has no absolute obedience and no backup (V06 p-005, VIK-065); reproducibility is not identity; operational sacrifice of Sirins coexists with apology to an individual one (V06 p-006, VIK-078); chosen self-risk is distinct from deciding that someone else is expendable (V13 p-005, VIK-177); a servant family has reason to hate him (Alter.1 part0046); and his status changes what a gift means (part0057). It names the failure mode: reaching the ethical question after technical feasibility. B would overclaim: the profile describes the deliberation that would settle a new case (whether he establishes standing) only as a developmental trend, and the generalization of his creator ethics beyond an attached subject is MODERATE. D would understate argued, located positions with a named failure mode and located repairs.

The profile gives the comic engines of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk): hypercompetence as setup and ordinary irritation as punchline, insult as familiarity (七歳児 to Lerche, V05 p-005, VIK-024), family preemption of his loopholes (V06 p-009, VIK-084), competitive pique at chess with Shin (Shinei Nouzen) (Alter.1 part0041, VIK-195 to VIK-196) and dry social observation that sits beside accurate perception. It bounds them: he sometimes loses the exchange, and his roughness should not be softened. C would understate functional forms with located controls. A is rejected: the V12 caterpillar impulse and the teasing of Lerche past V05 have no listed control, and there is no stated suspension rule beyond the attachment-fear and trauma states.

A dedicated canonical profile of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) over V05-V14 and Alter.1. The profile says its index holds 205 rows, but in the set itself are 22 control entries naming 35 rows, each routed only to volume and XHTML file, one with a Phase-5 locator (V13-L061) and two only as a row's vicinity. V08 (20 index rows) and V11 (9) have no listed control, and several claims (the caterpillar, Zelene, a speaking Legion intelligence, the Annette (Annette Penrose) relation, battle anger) have none. C would overclaim: a reviewer cannot reach a single paragraph from the set, the other 170 rows sit in the uncurated index, and the narrower authorities that govern conflicts (L01, L02, L09, Documents 08 and 12) are outside the set. E would understate a dedicated profile whose file-routed controls reach every developmental state it names across seven volumes and Alter.1.

For Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) there are ten dispositioned counterexamples, thirteen mischaracterization traps and seventeen would-sound-wrong constraints. Located negatives include the absence of absolute obedience and of a backup for Lerche (V06 p-005, VIK-065) against 'uniform cruelty' and against 'benevolent creator' alike, the operational sacrifice of Sirins with apology (V06 p-006, VIK-078), the V14 trauma response against 'fearless' (p-006, VIK-184), そう在りたい against 'pure dynastic captive' (V07 p-007, VIK-091), the chess loss against 'omnipotent genius' (Alter.1 part0041) and the profile's ruling that his reading of Shin (Shinei Nouzen) is a hypothesis, not omniscience. C would understate affirmative, located constraints. A is rejected: no control reaches a paragraph, several constraints rest on the canonical V06 reading outside the set, and limits after V14 are open.

States of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) are each located by volume and XHTML file (V05 p-002 to p-010, V06 p-005 to p-009, V07 p-007, V09 p-004, V12 p-008, V13 p-005, V14 p-006), with the childhood and Lercheritt material placed as memory. B would overclaim: no control reaches a paragraph, order inside a volume is given only by file sequence, V08 and V11 have no listed control, no default state is named, and V05-V06 is a grouped phase for the creator turn. D would understate a seven-state sequence located by file with one Phase-5 locator.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation, with 俺 as first person and an aristocratic-intellectual register over a blunt masculine frame; never permanently ceremonial royal speech.

Address uses only attested forms by frame: 卿 for officers and peers in an aristocratic-professional frame, お前 in familiar or command contexts, 貴様 under irritation or battle pressure, and rough familiarity such as 七歳児 with Lerche; no invented honorific system or sentence-final habit.
Technical content becomes more exact, not more polite, and the deepest attachment lines become simpler, not more eloquent.
No frequency distribution, anime performance or state after V14 is claimed, and output that depends on one abstains.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence constrains pronoun, address, register shifts and the simplification rule enough for illustrative output with sampled recipients. The absence of a sentence-ending profile and paragraph-located exemplars restricts form and confidence rather than blocking use.

conditions: Chronology is one explicitly selected present state: V05; V06 after the Lerche and Shin (Shinei Nouzen) exchanges (p-005 to p-006); V07 after p-007; V09 after p-004; V12; V13 after p-005; or V14 after p-006. Childhood and Lercheritt material is memory in every state, V08 and V11 are not used, nothing after V14 is used, and Alter.1 does not fix a state.

The interlocutor is a profiled relation in its attested register: Lerche, Shin, Lena (Vladilena Milizé), Zafar (Zafar Idinarohk), Frederica (Frederica Rosenfort), the Eighty-Six or an individual Sirin in a combat frame. Annette (Annette Penrose), his father as policy authority, Zelene and unfamiliar persons are a separate, lower-confidence condition.

The situation matches a sampled class: a technical or battlefield anomaly, a peer's self-defeating premise, a refusal by Lerche, sacrifice or loss of a Sirin, a family prohibition, a political stake for allies, a status-loaded ordinary gesture, competitive leisure, or a trauma cue.

Output predicts his characteristic errors and overreach (reaching ethics after feasibility, contemptuous diagnosis that wounds, loophole-hunting, pettiness) as well as his restraints, and never makes him emotionless, secretly normal or omniscient.

It abstains on research or creator choices about a person or artificial subject he has no attachment to and no accepted authority over, on Sirin institutional redesign, on his postwar role and on any romance.

The profile affirmatively leaves romance open for Vika (Viktor Idinarohk): any canonical romantic relationship is OPEN, his marriage is dynastically constrained (V07 p-007, VIK-088), the master-servant bond with Lercheritt is not to be romanticized, and it forbids inferring romance from loss, proximity or the negative evidence that he has kissed neither Lercheritt nor Lerche. CONDITIONAL would require settling what the profile leaves open.

conditions: His domains are Sirin and artificial-person architecture, weapons and battlefield systems, strategy and royal politics, with neural-interface and Para-RAID research the stronger domain of Annette (Annette Penrose); sampled conduct includes the Sirin design choices (V06 p-005), command and apology in combat (V06 p-006), the V13 political stake (p-005) and command under V14 trauma (p-006).
Decisions isolate the governing mechanism, discard irrelevant convention and exploit the remaining constraint; reasoning is compressed and may read as arrogant.
Research choices over unattached persons and any institutional role after V14 are not modeled.

known_limits.statement: The source boundary is locked original-Japanese V01-V14 for Vika (Viktor Idinarohk), materially from V05, with Alter.1 supplemental and Alter.2 excluded. His V15+ development, postwar role, the fate of the Sirin institution and any romance are OPEN in the profile.

How far the creator restraint of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) generalizes from Lerche to artificial persons he has no attachment to, whether it would produce institutional redesign, and whether he accepts peer constraints in a high-stakes scientific dispute are MODERATE in the profile; the deciding question of standing versus feasibility is described only as a developmental trend.

The readings that Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) gives of other people, including Shin (Shinei Nouzen), are hypotheses from partial analogy in the profile, not omniscient access, and output must not make him automatically right about people.
Current Lerche is not Lercheritt restored, and feeling of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) toward one is not to be assumed identical to feeling toward the other.

The profile of Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) is a derived reconstruction reference whose header subordinates it to the Japanese source and the narrower canonical V2 authorities (L01, L02, L09 and the thematic Documents), none of which is curated on this row. It names its cumulative index as the retrieval surface for exact anchors; that index is not curated here.
No listed control for Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) is routed to a paragraph, two are given only as a row's vicinity, and V08 and V11 have no listed control, so states in those volumes cannot be selected.

The profile gives no sentence-ending, particle or lexicon profile for Vika (Viktor Idinarohk) and makes no claim about performed voice; voice claims cover pronoun, address and register shifts in written Japanese only.
